Gunpowder, also called black powder, is a chemical mixture that burns very rapidly, producing hot gases that can propel objects or create explosive effects.Traditionally, it consists of three main ingredients:
 

%c[ui_gray_3]PROPERTIES:
 - Potassium nitrate (saltpeter) : Supplies oxygen to support rapid burning.
 - Charcoal : Acts as the primary fuel
 - Sulfur : Helps the mixture ignite more easily and burn more efficiently.

A Full Metal Jacket (FMJ) bullet is a type of projectile where a soft lead core is enclosed by a harder metal jacket, typically made from copper or a copper alloy. The jacket usually covers the sides and nose of the bullet, while the base may or may not be exposed, depending on the design.:
 

%c[ui_gray_3]PROPERTIES:
 - Metal jacket – Reduces barrel fouling, improves feeding reliability, and helps the bullet maintain its shape.
 - Lead core – Provides most of the bullet's mass.
 - Optional exposed base – Many FMJ bullets have a small exposed lead base; some "total metal jacket" (TMJ) bullets completely enclose the lead core.

A Hollow Point (HP) bullet is a projectile with a small cavity (hollow) in the tip. This cavity is designed so that, when the bullet strikes a soft target, the front of the bullet expands or "mushrooms.":
 

%c[ui_gray_3]PROPERTIES:
 - Copper or copper-alloy jacket
 - Lead core.
 - Hollow cavity in the nose.

An Armor-Piercing (AP) bullet is a projectile designed to penetrate hard barriers, such as certain types of armor or other hardened materials, more effectively than a conventional bullet. Rather than relying mainly on expansion or deformation, its effectiveness comes from a very hard, dense core that resists flattening on impact.
 

%c[ui_gray_3]PROPERTIES:
 - Outer jacket – Usually copper or a copper alloy.
 - Hardened penetrator core – Commonly made from hardened steel, tungsten alloy, or (historically) other very dense materials.
 - Optional lead filler – Some designs include lead around the core to help fill the jacket.

Buckshot is a type of shotgun ammunition that contains multiple large spherical pellets inside a single shell instead of one single projectile. When a shotgun is fired, the shell releases these pellets, which spread out as they travel. The amount of spread depends on the distance and the shotgun's barrel and choke.:\n \n
A slug (or shotgun slug) is a single, large projectile fired from a shotgun. Unlike birdshot or buckshot, which contain many pellets, a slug shell contains one solid projectile. \n \n
Birdshot is a type of shotgun ammunition that contains many small spherical pellets packed inside a single shotgun shell. \n \n
Casing for Medium and Large Caliber

An ammo casing, more accurately called a cartridge case, is the container that holds the components of a cartridge together. It is not the bullet—it's the part that's left behind after the bullet leaves the barrel. \n \n

A primer is the small ignition component in the base of a cartridge. Its job is to ignite the propellant (typically smokeless powder) when the firearm is fired.The primer does not provide the main force that launches the bullet. Instead, it creates a small, hot flame that ignites the propellant, which then produces the gases that propel the projectile. \n \n
